title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: scope policies to users with adaptive scopes
summary: Hold: the proposed policy-scoping PowerShell operation has undocumented parameter semantics, while Microsoft's setup guidance says to manage these policies in the portal. The membership command also needs a current-member filter, and the briefing incorrectly extends a licensing warning about Exchange validation results to actual scope membership.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: New-SupervisoryReviewRule -Policy <PolicyIdParameter> -IncludeAdaptiveScopes <String[]> is a documented operation for configuring adaptive scoping of a Communication Compliance policy.
claims.quote: Searched: '"New-SupervisoryReviewRule" "IncludeAdaptiveScopes" Communication Compliance'; opened new-supervisoryreviewrule and communication-compliance-configure. Syntax exists, but the parameter description is a placeholder; setup says policy management cannot use PowerShell.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and replace the corresponding rendered command with Not yet documented. Add to its note: 'The PowerShell reference lists -IncludeAdaptiveScopes without documenting its behavior; the setup guide says to create and manage Communication Compliance policies in the portal.' Retain https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-supervisoryreviewrule and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure as sources for that qualification. The missing Name parameter is not the finding.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Adaptive scope queries are configured through Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal ... **Settings** ... **Roles and scopes** ... **Adaptive scopes**. ... select **+ Create scope**. ... Select the type of scope, and then select the attributes or properties you want to use to build the dynamic membership.
claims.fix: Keep the documented entry path, but add to controls[1].note and the rendered note: 'Continue through the scope configuration, keep Full directory when not restricting by administrative units, select Users or Microsoft 365 Groups, and configure the attributes and values or select Advanced query builder.' The printed path currently stops at the wizard entry rather than the query configuration.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate adaptive-scoping charge or meter in the reviewed Communication Compliance licensing and billing documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: '"adaptive scopes" "Communication Compliance" "billing" "price"'; read the Purview service description, adaptive scopes page and setup billing section. Billing is described for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, not for selecting adaptive scopes.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Users without a valid adaptive-scopes licence do not have the policy settings applied.
claims.quote: When you use these commands to validate a user scope, if the number of recipients returned is higher than expected, it might be because it includes users who don't have a valid license for adaptive scopes. These users don't have the policy settings applied to them.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions: licensing
claims.claim: Unlicensed users appear in the actual adaptive scope membership even though the policy does not cover them.
claims.quote: Searched: '"adaptive scope" "unlicensed" "members"'; read adaptive scopes validation and membership details and Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers. The licensing warning concerns Exchange validation-command results, not a guarantee about actual scope membership.
claims.fix: Replace 'so a scope can list people the policy does not cover' with 'Exchange query-validation results can include unlicensed users to whom policy settings do not apply.' Replace the After rollout bullet with 'Investigate unlicensed users returned by Exchange query validation; those results are not proof that policy settings apply.' In the licensing open question, replace 'list scope members it excludes' with 'distinguish unlicensed users in Exchange validation results'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes#validate-advanced-queries.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: No new data is read.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Communication Compliance adaptive scopes no new data read query values warning automatic remediation' and '"Communication Compliance" "adaptive scopes" "no new data"'; read adaptive scopes and policy setup. Neither states this blanket data-access assurance.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new data is read.' Keep the narrower explanation that an adaptive scope defines the users or groups a policy covers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An existing policy's conditions remain unchanged when adaptive scopes are used.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Communication Compliance" "adaptive scopes" "data" "conditions"' and 'Communication compliance adaptive scopes change existing policy all users edit'; read policy settings and custom-policy setup. They describe separate configuration, not this change guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace 'the policy's conditions and locations are unchanged' with 'the policy wizard configures locations and conditions separately from the user selection'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure#step-5-required-create-a-communication-compliance-policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An existing policy's locations remain unchanged when adaptive scopes are used.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Communication Compliance" "adaptive scopes" "data" "conditions"' and 'Communication compliance adaptive scopes change existing policy all users edit'; read policy settings and custom-policy setup. No passage guarantees existing locations are preserved by a switch.
claims.fix: Use the same single replacement for the shared clause: 'the policy wizard configures locations and conditions separately from the user selection'. Do not imply that changing an existing policy to adaptive scoping has documented preservation behavior. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure#step-5-required-create-a-communication-compliance-policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Remediation stays with human investigators rather than adaptive scopes taking automatic remediation actions.
claims.quote: Investigators have a range of actions they can take to address the displayed message and no automatic actions are taken without manual investigator review.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-solution-overview#system-capabilities to sources for the statement that remediation requires investigator review.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Advanced user or group queries can be validated with Get-Recipient or Get-Mailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use either Get-Recipient, Get-Mailbox, or Get-User with the -Filter parameter and your OPATH query for the adaptive scope enclosed in curly brackets ... Get-Mailbox doesn't support the MailUser recipient type, so you must use Get-Recipient or Get-User

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Mistyped query values always fail silently, with no warning or notification that coverage is wrong.
claims.quote: Searched: '"adaptive scopes" "warning" "values"' and 'Communication Compliance adaptive scopes no new data read query values warning automatic remediation'; read adaptive scopes configuration and validation. No immediate value validation is documented, not a blanket absence of warnings.
claims.fix: Remove 'and nobody is told' from Why it matters. Replace 'Query errors fail silently: a valid but wrong value returns an empty or partial scope with no warning' with 'Query values are not validated immediately because the query does not run immediately'. In the risk rationale replace 'silently leaves users unmonitored' with 'can leave intended users outside the scope'. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes#configure-adaptive-scopes.

claims.where: Governance controls: closing paragraph
claims.claim: An adaptive scope is a reusable configuration element that can be used by Communication Compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy. ... As a reusable configuration element, the same adaptive scope can be used for other compliance policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security
claims.claim: Policy populations update automatically as users match the configured attribute criteria rather than requiring repeated static-list updates.
claims.quote: With adaptive policy scopes, policies are automatically updated to include users that match defined risk criteria rather than requiring admins to repeatedly update static lists of users to include in the policy scope.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check whether Communication Compliance administrators are restricted by admin units ... Controls rows cover adaptive policy selection, scope queries, membership and role-group membership; none provides the administrative-unit assignment control.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step asking administrators to check administrative-unit restrictions has no corresponding control row. Remove that checklist step; retain the documented restriction in Scope and the policy row's note. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
